content: Older adults diagnosed with diabetes should adhere to an optimal nutritional plan that includes adequate protein intake to support their overall health. Engaging in regular physical activity is crucial, with a focus on aerobic exercises, weight-bearing activities, and balance training to preserve functional capacity and prevent physical decline. A modest weight loss of 5–7% of body weight should be considered, as it has been shown to improve quality of life and reduce cardiometabolic risks. Lifestyle management, which encompasses a balanced diet and consistent exercise, is essential for older adults to prevent frailty, enhance muscle strength, and lower the risk of falls and functional deterioration. Structured programs that emphasize dietary modifications and physical activity have demonstrated significant benefits, including reductions in body weight and blood pressure, as well as improvements in physical performance. These interventions collectively contribute to an enhanced quality of life for older adults.
